channel.title: Queering Earth — the accession register
channel.description: Every sheet as it was mounted, every plate that came off again, and every label we corrected — the register's own accessions, reasoning included. New pages alone are a separate feed at https://queering.earth/feed.xml. Generated from the register itself by tools/make-markdown.mjs.

item.title: Two of the five link relations this site sent were not relations at all
item.description: Label corrected: The header said registered relation types only and two of the five were not Label corrected: The second one was the one nearly missed

item.title: A gate that counts closing tags, and the eight attributions it found wearing their emphasis inside out
item.description: Cabinet: Check 9: every element closes, and closes in order Label corrected: Eight attributions had their bold and their italic closed in the wrong order Label corrected: An open question about a 1922 printing had been bold to the end of its own paragraph Cabinet: Made to fail in three shapes before being believed

item.title: A page that says what arrived, two feeds instead of one, and a date that could not be taken from this register
item.description: Mounted: The cabinet by date, at /whats-new Cabinet: The feed existed, and nothing on the site linked to it Cabinet: One feed became two, because they are two lists for two readers Label corrected: An accession on this page had no closing tag, and the feed had been dropping one ever since Cabinet: This register cannot say when a page was made, and that was measured rather than assumed

item.title: Two van Goghs, two recordings, and a privacy page that had a number in it
item.description: Mounted: Two paintings, and two recordings that fetch nothing until pressed Label corrected: The privacy page stops counting Cabinet: No lyric was quoted, for two different reasons

item.title: Sheet No. 11, and four biographies that would not say what they were supposed to
item.description: Mounted: My Gloomy Sunflowers Re-determined: Galveston was 1964, the diagnosis was not manic depression, and it was the Army Label corrected: Which ever, two words

item.title: One typeface was too wide for the masthead, and the gate had been rendering one of ten states
item.description: Label corrected: Sporting Grotesque is set smaller, and the number is a measurement whose expected answer was wrong Cabinet: The width gate renders ten states now, and reads the face list from the table that owns it

item.title: The masthead had been 34px right of centre since the day it was drawn
item.description: Label corrected: A centring rule that stops working when the sign changes

item.title: A word one syllable from the right one, and it belonged to Bowlby
item.description: Label corrected: Monotropism is Dinah Murray’s; monotropy is John Bowlby’s, and they are not the same word shortened

item.title: The masthead read Queering.Ear / th, and the measurement that certified it was of the wrong thing
item.description: Label corrected: The rule was right and the scope was wrong

item.title: Three pages had been scrolling sideways since the day each was mounted, and a ninth gate to say so
item.description: Label corrected: A string with no break opportunity breaks the page instead Label corrected: The plate’s frame bled into a gutter that paper does not have Cabinet: A ninth gate, which could have failed on three pages the hour before it was written

item.title: A fair-use position, written down before the sheet that needs it
item.description: Mounted: What we quote, and why we may Cabinet: A seventh page in the drawer, and a fourteenth link in the row

item.title: Three drawers, a breadcrumb on every sheet, and a panel that moved when a control was added
item.description: Mounted: Three collection pages, and not one of them repeats a sentence the home page already carries Mounted: The breadcrumb was already here, one crumb long, on twelve pages Label corrected: The readings drawer answered to three names, and two of them were older than the drawer Cabinet: The three drawers joined the footer row, and their labels are the one place a short label is not allowed Label corrected: The home page said eight sheets, and the plate has held ten since 10 September Cabinet: A panel hung off its own control moves when a control is added, and the one that moved was the old one

item.title: A masthead for the two modes, and the width a masthead is actually reviewed at
item.description: Mounted: One flower against many, with the two flower areas equal by computation Label corrected: A masthead is reviewed at 448px, not at the 34rem measure — a number this register already held Cabinet: Three more refused drawings, one of them this file’s own recorded mistake repeated

item.title: Two Bewick cuts from 1792, and a masthead refused twice
item.description: Mounted: Thomas Bewick engraved both animals for one 1792 volume, and his prose is as good as his cuts Cabinet: A blown-up tray mark is not a masthead, and that is favicon.svg’s rule running the other way

item.title: Every poem on the site was arriving in the Markdown mirror as prose
item.description: Label corrected: A verse line is the one span on this site that is not a bare wrapper Mounted: The hard break is a backslash, because two trailing spaces would have been erased after they were written

item.title: A third founding paper, on the fox and the hedgehog, and an unlabelled door in the top bar
item.description: Mounted: Two children’s poems that end in the same place, which is the argument Mounted: The anthology has no fox, so the fox came from the oldest nursery collection in English Mounted: The 1922 edition prints runts and digs, and we went to the letterforms to be sure Label corrected: A journal credits a review to the author of the book it reviews, and dates a poet two centuries wrong Mounted: The fox-and-hedgehog mark, and why the two of them do not face each other Cabinet: Found and deliberately not fixed: the Markdown mirror flattens every poem on the site into prose Cabinet: The controls tray wraps, because a fifth control would have scrolled the body sideways

item.title: One sentence of Max Alexander pasted up as a broadside, and the rule that a component mixes type roles and never families
item.description: Mounted: A broadside: one sentence, six lines, six sizes, and not a word of it altered Mounted: A component may mix the two type roles; it may never name a family Mounted: Plain view keeps the composition and drops the ornament, which is a split the cut-out line already drew

item.title: Sheet No. 10, on a disability invented because nobody had it, and the readers who do
item.description: Mounted: The argument is not that Schalk is wrong, and finding the version that is not cheap took the whole research pass Mounted: One sprig drawn twice and translated, because a mirrored pair says reflection and this is not a reflection Label corrected: A quotation arrived under the wrong Butler novel, at a page number that was not a page number Label corrected: The empathy study is a 2024 article behind a 2023 DOI, and its accepted manuscript is not quotable Label corrected: Two glossary pages of our own splice two Butler passages ninety pages apart into one quotation Mounted: A section that argues against the sheet it is on

item.title: Sheet No. 9, on a definition recited for a beast nobody has seen, and on the coiner an empty word leaves behind
item.description: Mounted: The primary was not in the house, and the answer was the French rather than a summary Mounted: Five mounting straps and no specimen, after the diagonal version was drawn, measured, and thrown away Mounted: The unmended provenance line ships for the first time, on the ninth sheet Mounted: Two of Henry Holiday’s 1876 engravings, one of which is an empty square and the other of which is the Snark wearing a wig Label corrected: The story everybody tells about Carroll refusing the Boojum drops three words, and the three words are the point Cabinet: A half-hour reading of the poem is linked and not embedded, and the reader is named Label corrected: A sentence of Carroll’s preface is quoted around rather than repaired Cabinet: The masthead’s own borrowed coinage is now a section of a sheet, not just a ledger entry

item.title: A crooked tree for the sheet that says queering is adaptation, and the stump of the straight one beside it
item.description: Mounted: The drawing is the pair, because a crooked tree on its own is only a picture of a crooked tree Label corrected: Four words have an author, and we do not know whose these are

item.title: Nine typefaces a reader can set the sheet in, six of them drawing letters that exist because the grammar refused the person
item.description: Mounted: A typeface picker where four options set the reading face and five only set the headings, and that split is a constraint rather than a taste Cabinet: CUTE is not the OFL, and reading it is what turned up two faults in our own house

item.title: The device decides, and the reader may say otherwise: three reading settings, and a motion rule that had to be turned inside out to allow the second answer
item.description: Label corrected: The fonts were redistributed for a day with no licence beside them, and their designers were credited to a search engine Label corrected: The panel shipped unable to open, and every test that passed had bypassed the thing that was broken Mounted: Reduce motion, more contrast and looser lines, each starting from what the device already asks for Cabinet: Text size, which the sheet already followed — and the first setting that is not a yes or a no Re-determined: Motion is off by default now, and the rule that guarded it came out of the change stronger than it went in Cabinet: Forced colours, which is the one setting here that is not ours to offer — and a gate that makes /privacy name every key the site keeps

item.title: The manifesto, adapted under its own licence — and a tightened quotation found on our own foundation’s page while sourcing it
item.description: Label corrected: One preposition and an undeclared ellipsis, in the version of Max Alexander this site was handed Mounted: Two quotations that cannot be verified, carried anyway, with the transcription named instead of the tape Cabinet: Two of the nine authors wrote this page, which is exactly why the credit is not a formality

item.title: A new accession goes at the top, anchored on the register, and this one proves it
item.description: Cabinet: The fixed anchor cannot go wrong whoever else is editing; the relative one is correct only while nobody is

item.title: A way straight to the newest accession, and the discovery that it was not where the page said it was
item.description: Mounted: The address is on the register, not on the newest accession, which is what makes it permanent Label corrected: Four accessions written after 22:43 were sitting below four written before it Cabinet: Two assertions on the register’s order, and only one of them would have caught this

item.title: The finding aid gets one too, and three thresholds in a row turn out to have been the same mistake
item.description: Cabinet: Three thresholds tried, three retired, each measuring the list instead of the reader Label corrected: Straight after the lede put the search box below the fold, on the page that is a search box

item.title: This register now has the contents list an earlier entry measured, refused, and wrote a rule against
item.description: Re-determined: Block height was the wrong measure, the same way heading count was the wrong measure an hour ago

item.title: A feature was mistaken for a fault, removed, and put back within the hour
item.description: Label corrected: The test is the element now, not the class, so the next navigation block needs no line Re-determined: It was not a fault. Ryan liked the rail pointing at the index, and a destination inside a nav is still a destination Mounted: And the two record pages got the contents list they could not have had an hour earlier Cabinet: The two-heading threshold is retired, because it measured the wrong thing Label corrected: The removal also broke the rail’s tick scale in the quietest way available, because the derivation existed twice

item.title: The two longest pages on the site could not be surveyed without reading all of them
item.description: Mounted: Back matter again, and built at runtime for the reason the contents list is Cabinet: No line in REVEAL, and that was checked rather than assumed

item.title: Two pages of this cabinet had addresses, were listed on the home page, and were reachable from the foot of nothing
item.description: Cabinet: Eighty copies of five sentences, and the one place they were supposed to live Cabinet: Where a sheet says which copy it read, and why that is not the provenance line

item.title: A way back to the top, drawn as growth rather than as a chevron
item.description: Cabinet: The arrowhead is a seed head, because a chevron laid over grass is an interface arrow in a costume Label corrected: The landmark could not take focus, and the skip link had wanted it to since the day it was written

item.title: Sheet No. 2 had no lede and an essay with no heading, so its own contents list could not name the reason it exists
item.description: Label corrected: A heading in the author’s own words, and a note that stopped being true the moment anything sat above the essay

item.title: The plate was eight screens down its own home page and there was no way back up to it
item.description: Cabinet: Two contents lists on one screen, on purpose, and the argument for why they are not the same object Cabinet: The rule that says grow the hit area was followed with the wrong instrument, and then with the wrong arithmetic Cabinet: Built at runtime is free; hidden is not, and the rail was both in the same afternoon Label corrected: The rail would not appear for the person who asked for it, and the number keeping it away had been reserving room for a block that is not there Cabinet: The rail’s ticks became a scale drawing of the sheet, because an imperfection with no norm behind it just reads as an accident Cabinet: The rail’s rule ends in a leaf now, and the doodles that were asked for were drawn and refused Label corrected: This register said a rule did nothing, having measured it on screen and never on paper Cabinet: Three sheets had no contents list and no reason for not having one

item.title: The ledger and the decision log had no addresses, so the aim that pointed at them was the thinnest receipt on the mission page
item.description: Mounted: A generator that runs backwards, because the Markdown is the thing being kept and the page is the copy Cabinet: The addresses are not /attributions and /decisions, and that is a filesystem fact rather than a preference Label corrected: The finding aid was describing a smaller cabinet than it searches Cabinet: Both walkers learned a tag on the same afternoon, and one of them had to learn not to tidy

item.title: A cabinet that publishes an attribution ledger, a privacy policy and a register of its own errors had never written down what any of it was for
item.description: Mounted: Thirteen aims, each naming the page already keeping it — and, for each, the observation that would falsify it Mounted: Two quotations from our own two organisations, held to the standard everybody else’s words are held to Cabinet: The Markdown converter now honours a list’s start attribute, because thirteen aims in four groups renumbered themselves four times

item.title: An eighth gate, ported the same day the failure it catches happened twice — and its first honest run found fifteen more
item.description: Cabinet: The upstream tool would have certified the exact plate that prompted it, and finding that out was most of the port Label corrected: Fifteen cards called a sheet something the plate does not call it, including an essay filed as a reading Cabinet: What it refuses to check, and the one that looks most like an omission

item.title: The plate said seven and carried eight, and two of them were in the wrong order — on the one page whose job is to say what is here
item.description: Label corrected: Eight, and in order — the count above the plate and the sequence on it Label corrected: The same fault, found by looking for it: one sibling nav ran 4, 1, 2, 3

item.title: The four pages that are not specimens were only ever in the footer, which is where a site puts what it hopes nobody needs
item.description: Mounted: A list with no cards, because a card would say these were readings and none of them is a reading of anything Cabinet: The target is the line and not the letters, which is the rule the ground control shipped one pixel over

item.title: A site that had spent a day removing its only third-party request mounted a YouTube player, and the whole of the work was making that honest
item.description: Mounted: A facade, not an embed: the served page holds a drawing and a link, and nothing reaches Google until somebody presses play Cabinet: The gate now reads our JavaScript, because section 7 looked only at markup and a script is where a third party would actually appear Label corrected: Five statements on the privacy page stopped being true on the same afternoon, and all five were corrected in the change that broke them

item.title: A lilac bush from Ryan’s own yard, standing above the footer, and the song under it belongs to a man almost nobody names
item.description: Mounted: The vase habit is the whole read, and two drafts got it wrong in the same way Cabinet: Eighty-five kilobytes of markup, nine over the wire — and the trick that would have shrunk it breaks the styling silently Mounted: Helen hears Eliot the instant anybody says lilac, so the plate got the four lines that come with the flower Label corrected: Lilac Wine is James Shelton’s, and the caption says so before it names either singer

item.title: A moth with the Earth where its body should be, in somebody else’s two colours, and the hardest part was stopping the middle of it from looking like a brain
item.description: Mounted: The drawing is at the foot of a section rather than at the top of a page, which is the first time anything here has been Cabinet: Two new decorative tokens, because a wash and the thing washed onto it cannot be one value Cabinet: The coastlines are projected rather than drawn, because three passes of hand-drawn continents kept reading as a brain

item.title: A real herbarium stamps its sheets with an accession number that is a row in a ledger, which is the whole reason this one could have it and most of the work was proving the ink was legal
item.description: Mounted: Every sheet is stamped, and the fade is on the ring because no colour here can make a letter faint and legal Cabinet: The washed-out effect is a blend mode, the blend mode erases the stamp in the drawer, and the contrast gate reported it clean Label corrected: The stylesheet was cached for five minutes longer than the markup that needed it, and the first reader of the stamp saw the consequence Cabinet: A seventh gate, ported because a design was refused for want of it — and it measures paper, which the tool it came from does not Cabinet: A sixth gate, because a comment in a config file predicted this failure and a comment cannot fail a build Cabinet: The finding aid does not index the stamp, which is the masthead decision arriving one component further down

item.title: A cabinet made almost entirely of other people’s sentences grew a search field, which is a machine for trimming other people’s sentences, and most of the work was teaching it when to refuse
item.description: Mounted: A finding aid that will show you a whole quotation or none of it Cabinet: The finding aid was nine thousand words down, and the control that fixes that is a drawing of a pocket lens Label corrected: The privacy policy said there was nowhere on this site to type anything, and then there was Cabinet: The gold stayed on the mend, and the mark that says found went onto a rule

item.title: The site was measured against somebody else’s specification, and the first thing it found was a defect this cabinet had already named, already fixed one layer up, and never thought to look for underneath
item.description: Mounted: A privacy policy, and the one third-party request it would have had to confess Cabinet: The plates are AVIF now, and the manuscript that cost 312 KB costs 34 Cabinet: Thirty days for the plates, five minutes for the stylesheet, and a promise we declined to make Cabinet: The site now says out loud, to machines, the permission it had only ever said to people — and puts the citation trail within reach of anything that takes it up Cabinet: A mistyped address no longer ejects the reader from the herbarium, and fixing it introduced a soft 404 the new gate caught Cabinet: One address per sheet at last, and a fourth gate that asks the site instead of the files Cabinet: Two response headers the site had simply never sent, and a policy that carries exactly one directive on purpose

item.title: Fifteen panels wore the specimen’s clothes, twenty-five margin values passed for a hand-kept register, and the site’s gold was being spent on the least interesting thing that happens to a sheet
item.description: Mounted: Every sheet now says when it was mounted and how often it has been corrected since Re-determined: The gold moved off mounting and onto the mend, and the drawing at the top of this page moved with it Cabinet: Three surfaces, because fifteen components were sharing one and a reader could only rank them by reading the label Label corrected: Dropping a fill from two panels took their list markers down to 3.89:1, and the fix was the rule this stylesheet already states everywhere else Cabinet: Space is a scale now, because twenty-five unrelated margin values do not read as a hand-kept register — they read as noise Cabinet: The foxing was pinned to the window while the paper moved under it, and all nine sheets were stained identically Mounted: Long sheets carry a contents list, every section has an address you can share, and the register has the addresses but not the list Cabinet: Every section on the site has an address now, and the home page still has no contents list, because its contents list is the plate Mounted: The Preferred Flower of Life — Sheet No. 8, and the first that is a wall rather than a reading Label corrected: A much-quoted Mary Oliver sentence is in the wrong book and is missing the half that answers it, and it took owning both books to find out Re-determined: Woolf’s resonant and porous is exactly right, and it is Woolf guessing at what Coleridge meant Label corrected: A 2005 paper’s byline deadnames its third author, and a citation generated from the record repeats it Cabinet: The card generator reported a hand-kept list of files rather than the files it wrote, and the new card went missing from its own summary Mounted: The register is indexed by sheet at the foot of the page, because a contents list is front matter and an index is back matter Cabinet: A fourth guard, because a mistyped sheet name drops an entry out of the index and leaves the page reading perfectly Cabinet: The register looked like the strongest case for a contents list and measured as the worst one, so it was built, measured, and taken out again Mounted: The colophon scores this site against the seven principles, including the two it fails, and names what it cannot vouch for in them Label corrected: This entry claimed a source swapped one principle for another, which was written from memory and is not established Label corrected: Our own foundation published the line this site’s gold seam is built on, four months before we reinvented a near copy of it Cabinet: The guard now measures the number this house publishes, and it was raised on the day the gap was nearly spent Label corrected: The wash was made to tile so that no long sheet had clean paper through the middle, and it drew a visible line across the page at every repeat

item.title: The sheet has a second ground, and it is the drawer shut rather than the lamp switched off
item.description: Cabinet: Brown rather than green, and the reason is measurable rather than a preference Cabinet: A card is lighter than the page in daylight and would be darker than it here, which is a trap and not a taste Cabinet: A discreet control, a machine that decides when nobody has, and paper that is daylight whatever either of them says Label corrected: Two claims about this site’s own measurements were describing the daylight sheet only, and one of them was describing a check that does not exist Cabinet: The guard measures both grounds, and it was made to fail before it was believed

item.title: A first-person account that ends the moment two words fit had nothing under it about what a word that fits is for, and the writers who answer that were gathered on Stimpunks pages that are a finding aid and not a citation
item.description: Mounted: Six sections below the essay, on what a label buys and what it charges Label corrected: The mounting label described a sheet that carried one text, and it now carries two Cabinet: Every quotation named to the copy it was read in, and a rule about our own library corrected in the middle of applying it

item.title: The most-quoted sentence about lavender and Abraham Lincoln is word for word what Carl Sandburg wrote, and the man it describes is Joshua Speed
item.description: Mounted: A Waste Garden, Flowering at Its Will — Sheet No. 7 Re-determined: The streak of lavender belongs to Joshua Speed, and only the referent has moved Cabinet: Two of the four plates are the wrong object, and both captions say so

item.title: Four flowers people wore when saying it in words was dangerous, drawn onto the corners of the plate of sheets
item.description: Cabinet: The border is an argument, and the line under it says whose set of four this is Cabinet: The frame is CSS and the corners are SVG, and the plate nearly became a list again

item.title: A heading that says the type plays was set in the same even measure as every other heading, which is a claim arguing against itself
item.description: Cabinet: The heading performs its own sentence, and the verb carries the axis wherever it is a heading

item.title: Higginson wrote let us alter as little as possible and then printed Dickinson’s poem with eight of its nine dashes gone — and the copy a reader will find today has lost a word out of the line that asks to be moored
item.description: Mounted: The Swell and the Dwell — Sheet No. 6 Re-determined: The poem in general circulation is missing the word but, and the page that prints it names no edition Re-determined: What 1891 did to the leaf, and the one change that is not a tidy Label corrected: Two scans agreed with each other and were both wrong, because they came out of the same library Label corrected: Three citations in the first draft of this sheet were written from memory, and one of them was an invented DOI Cabinet: A licensed plate for the first time, a title that breaks its own convention, and punctuation added to a poem of ours

item.title: A scholar cut her own sentence down to fit a later argument, marked every cut, and in doing so demonstrated the thing the sentence says
item.description: Mounted: Two sections on the front page: To queer is to adapt and The sentence adapts itself Cabinet: The second quotation is a trimmed version of the first, and that is why both are on the page Label corrected: Half of one quotation on this page has not been read against its primary, and the ledger says so

item.title: An editor in 1733 decided Miranda’s hardest speech was not credible coming from her, moved it into her father’s mouth, and three centuries of editions followed him
item.description: Mounted: Miranda: To Be Wondered With — Sheet No. 5 Label corrected: Two citations in the incoming draft, wrong before the sheet was ever built Cabinet: Four devices from Helen’s draft, kept — and its colours, not kept

item.title: A site that publishes a ledger of everyone else’s words was keeping the account of its own mistakes in a file only we could read
item.description: Cabinet: The register itself

item.title: A sheet shipped with Helen Edgar’s name over prose she did not write — she declined the credit, and the answer had been written in our own colophon before the sheet was made
item.description: Mounted: Wyrd, Weird, and the Invention of Normal — Sheet No. 4 Label corrected: The byline. It shipped wrong, and it was corrected on Helen’s word Re-determined: The sheet’s kind changed from essay to reading, and No. 1 gained a second reader Mounted: Two paintings, chosen by Helen Edgar Label corrected: A journal citation we were handed had the wrong issue and the wrong pages Label corrected: Two captions checked against the primary rather than against the picture Label corrected: A scholar’s conclusion that cuts against the sheet, kept on the sheet Cabinet: The paste-up: a zine wall built out of herbarium furniture Cabinet: The colophon says how these sheets are drafted

item.title: Two grey woodcuts came off a colour sheet, and the drawing above them was rebuilt twice before it stopped standing to attention
item.description: Re-determined: Colour over subject matter: three chromolithographs replace two Darwin woodcuts Label corrected: A digitiser’s metadata disagreed with the corner of the plate, for the third time Re-determined: The header drawing, rebuilt twice, and the first version was a fault rather than a preference

item.title: The first printing of Promises like Pie-crust ends line 20 with a colon, every copy in circulation ends it with a full stop, and the line is the one about breaking the chain
item.description: Mounted: The Die Uncast — Sheet No. 3 Label corrected: The colon at line 20, read in two separately scanned copies Label corrected: The proverb in the title has no owner here, on purpose Label corrected: Two elisions kept lower-case, and one character normalised with the reason written down Label corrected: A definition that circulates without a name got its name back Cabinet: Verse gets a shared component, and every line is its own element Cabinet: A sheet is titled from a phrase in the specimen, and the filename names the work

item.title: The site was linking to one address and declaring a different one canonical, and nobody would have found it by reading the repository
item.description: Cabinet: Addresses on this site are extensionless Cabinet: How this site is made — the colophon Cabinet: Sheets link to each other, outside the page’s main landmark

item.title: The phrase on the masthead turned out to be one hyphen away from the subtitle of a book we quote on the same page
item.description: Mounted: The Army of the Upright — Sheet No. 1 Mounted: Coming to Terms — Sheet No. 2 Label corrected: The masthead credits Nick Walker, and the decision log stopped claiming there was no risk Label corrected: The paraphrase that did not ship, and the pronouns that did Label corrected: Woolf verified ahead of the sheet, because this trap does not survive verification-after-drafting Mounted: Plate 511, The Floral Magazine v.9 (1870), and the first metadata error Cabinet: The plate, the favicon, and the social cards

item.title: For six minutes at a time the site looked deployed: a green dashboard, auto-publishing on, and a commit several pushes stale
item.description: Cabinet: The site is planted Cabinet: Continuous deployment, and the trap that made pushes silently not deploy Cabinet: queering.earth is live Cabinet: The content model: a sheet mounts a specimen and carries our label
